rows.definition: The cmd/fak/guard_mcp.go module: it wires fak's own MCP self-query surface (fak_index_*, fak_memory_*, fak_context_*) into the guarded child by injecting an MCP server registration into the child's launch config, mirroring the install shape of guard_precompact.go / guard_codex.go.
rows.distinction: guard_mcp is an INSTALL step of the guard wrapper (it edits the child's launch config before the child runs), not a decision gate that admits or refuses a call. Its OpenAI-Codex provider twin is guard_codex; guardMcpStatusAudit is the separate AUDIT that later checks the injection is actually live.

rows.definition: The cmd/fak/guard_codex.go module: the first-class `fak guard -- codex` wiring, fak's OpenAI-Codex provider install path (credential resolve plus config rewrite) that lets the guard front a Codex child the same way it fronts an Anthropic one.
rows.distinction: guard_codex is the Codex-PROVIDER install twin of guard_mcp and installGuardCodexConfig - a guard wrapper component, not a gate. installGuardCodexConfig is the specific routing-rewrite STEP it performs; guard_codex is the whole provider-install module around it.

rows.definition: assumecheck.GuardAssumption: the adjudication that folds a stated assumption plus its evidence into an Allow/Refuse verdict for `fak assume check` (and the re-witness loop `fak assume loop`).
rows.distinction: GuardAssumption is a guard-style ADJUDICATION over an assumption CLAIM (does the evidence witness it?), not a tool-call adjudicator like residencyGate and not a result admitter. It gates a claim's truth, not a syscall or its result; guardaccuracy scores a gate's decision, whereas GuardAssumption IS the decision over an assumption.

rows.definition: cmd/fak/guard_freshness.go guardUnattestedBuildWarning: the one-line WARN the guard BANNER prints under its build row when the running fak's build stamp is unattested or stale.
rows.distinction: It is a guard banner-render STRING, printed once at launch and then gone; its persistent twin is guardInfoStalenessNote, which carries the same staleness fact in the info pane. A banner note WARNS about provenance - it never refuses, so it is neither a guard system nor a gate.

rows.definition: cmd/fak/guard_freshness.go guardInfoStalenessNote: the guard INFO PANE's persistent twin of guardUnattestedBuildWarning - the build-staleness note rendered in the status overlay rather than the launch banner.
rows.distinction: Same staleness FACT as guardUnattestedBuildWarning, but rendered in the PERSISTENT guardInfo pane instead of the one-shot launch banner. Persistence (pane vs banner) is the whole distinction; both are render strings, neither is a gate.

rows.definition: cmd/fak/info_visual.go guardInfoVisualIdentityRow: the guard info block's header row - which fak this pane watches and for how long - rendered at the top of the guardInfo status overlay.
rows.distinction: A guardInfo PANE render row that IDENTIFIES the watched process (the block's header), distinct from guardInfoStalenessNote (which reports the build's freshness in the same pane). Identity header vs freshness note; both are pane rows, not gates.

rows.definition: cmd/fak/guard_pi.go installGuardPiExtension: rewrites a Pi child command to route through the gateway by installing a `-e <ext.ts>` provider-override extension, the Anthropic-wire twin of installGuardCodexConfig.
rows.distinction: The Pi-harness INSTALL twin of guard_mcp / installGuardCodexConfig - a guard wrapper install step that edits the child launch, not a gate that admits or refuses a call. It wires routing before the child runs; it makes no per-call decision.

rows.definition: cmd/fak/guard.go resolveGuardRemoteServe: resolves the base URL/target that `fak guard --remote-serve` binds and serves, delegating to resolveLabTarget.
rows.distinction: A guard STARTUP resolver that computes the guard's OWN serve endpoint, distinct from guardProvider, which resolves the UPSTREAM provider wire the guard forwards to. Own-endpoint vs upstream-endpoint; neither is a per-call gate.

rows.definition: cadencereport.CheckGateTriaged / milestonereport.CheckGateTriaged: a CI gate that passes only when every finding in a cadence/milestone report is triaged, returning a non-zero exit code otherwise.
rows.distinction: A report-boundary CI GATE (one report in, pass/fail out) that extends plain CheckGate with the TRIAGE-enforced condition. Its advisory (non-failing) counterpart is AdvisoryGateTriaged; a gate decides one report, it is not the guard system.

rows.definition: trendreport.AdvisoryGateTriaged: the ADVISORY form of the triaged gate - it emits a finding/verdict for an untriaged cadence or milestone report but does not fail the build unless enforcement is switched on.
rows.distinction: The advisory (warn) twin of CheckGateTriaged (refuse): same triage condition, but advisory reports never fail CI on their own. It mirrors the advisoryGate pattern - a report gate whose severity is downgraded to advisory until enforced.

rows.definition: metrics.GateSpendLabeled: a gate that refuses a spend rollup carrying unlabeled cost categories - every spend line must name its category - returning the offending defects.
rows.distinction: A metrics-hygiene GATE over a spend rollup (one report in, defects out), the spend twin of GateBudgetLabeled. It gates DATA labeling, not a tool call or its result, so it is neither an adjudicator nor a result admitter.

rows.definition: internal/hooks/gate_tierdeclared.go gateTierDeclaredTree: emits a TIER_DECLARED finding for every internal/<leaf> package across the WHOLE tracked tree that lacks a declared support tier.
rows.distinction: The WHOLE-TREE audit form of the leaf tier-declaration rule; its staged-diff twin is gateUntieredLeaf, which fires only on the leaves a commit stages. Same rule, tree-wide scope vs staged-diff scope.

rows.definition: internal/hooks/gate_untieredleaf.go gateUntieredLeaf: emits an UNTIERED_LEAF finding for every internal/<leaf> the STAGED diff touches without a declared support tier - the pre-commit boundary check.
rows.distinction: The staged-diff (pre-commit) twin of gateTierDeclaredTree: both enforce leaf tier-declaration, but gateUntieredLeaf gates only what a commit STAGES, while gateTierDeclaredTree audits the whole tree. Staged-scope vs tree-scope.

rows.definition: The FAK_ABLATE_PREFIX_GUARD env knob (internal/ablate, internal/gateway): when set, it DISABLES the cacheable-prefix stability guard so its value can be A/B measured by ablation.
rows.distinction: An ABLATION knob that turns the prefixGuard feature OFF, distinct from the feature itself (prefixGuard) and from its determinism-witness metric family fak_prefix_guard_*. This is the OFF switch, not the feature and not the counter.

rows.definition: The fak_prefix_guard_* metric family (internal/gateway, observePrefixGuard): the determinism witness that measures whether the cacheable prompt prefix is actually stable turn-to-turn.
rows.distinction: The MEASUREMENT/witness metric of the prefix guard (is the prefix stable?), distinct from the feature knob prefixGuard and its ablation switch FAK_ABLATE_PREFIX_GUARD. This is the counter that observes the guard, not the control that turns it on or off.

rows.definition: The FAK_PRESTAGED_PATH_GUARD env opt-out (internal/hooks/gate_barecommitsweep.go): the git-hook gate family that refuses committing paths staged outside the sanctioned by-path flow; setting it to `off` disables the whole family.
rows.distinction: A config OPT-OUT for a git-hook GATE family (the bare-commit / pre-staged-path sweep), distinct from ALLOW_BARE_COMMIT, which skips the check ONCE. FAK_PRESTAGED_PATH_GUARD=off disables the family; ALLOW_BARE_COMMIT=1 is a single-commit skip.
